[msg_fCVJ8JJwLqzLcSpF42pXjg | Reviewer] Diagnosis: the Windows breakage is caused by a Unix-style executable check being applied too early and too broadly. In `windows-enrollment`, `codex` is resolved with `exec.LookPath`, then rejected unless `os.Stat` succeeds and the file has an execute bit (`Mode().Perm() & 0o111 != 0`), which will reject Windows launchers and shims such as `codex.cmd` even when they are valid on Windows. In `windows-console-preflight`, the console also marks an agent `ExecutableReady` only through `executableAvailable(executablePath)` before any Runtime probe, so the agent can be reported unavailable before runtime validation. Evidence: [`windows-enrollment`](#) and [`windows-console-preflight`](#).

Minimal consistent policy:
- Keep discovery portable: continue using path resolution / lookup without executing anything.
- Make validation platform-aware:
  - Unix: require a regular file with an execute bit.
  - Windows: accept native launchers and shims that are launchable by the OS, including `.exe`, `.cmd`, `.bat`, and PATHEXT-resolved entries; do not require Unix permission bits.
- Keep Runtime permissions unchanged.

Checks to separate:
- Portable discovery check: “can the path be resolved?”
- Native-platform launchability check: “is this path a valid executable for the current OS?”

Missing evidence: the implementation of `executableAvailable` is not shown, so I cannot confirm whether the console preflight uses the same Unix-only rule or a different one.
